messages:
Anna: Heads-up — started onboarding `cetus-embed-6b` into staging for embeddings. Quick smoke run attached. Noticed a modest recall@1/5/10 drop vs our current `beacon-embed-v2`, and clustering silhouette looks lower. Posting raw run and short logs.

Vikram: thanks. can you paste the exact eval cmd you ran?

Anna: ran: ```bash
python eval/embeddings_eval.py --model cetus-embed-6b --quant int8 --holdout 10k --metrics recall@1,recall@5,recall@10,silhouette --norm l2 --similarity cosine
```

Anna: results: ```
baseline: beacon-embed-v2  recall@1=0.72  recall@5=0.85  recall@10=0.90  silhouette=0.34
cetus-embed-6b (int8) recall@1=0.65  recall@5=0.82  recall@10=0.88  silhouette=0.18
mean_cosine_shift = -0.032
short_query_recall_drop (qlen<=8) = -0.08
```

Tess: ouch silhouette drop is fairly large. did you normalize vectors before indexing? sometimes model outputs need explicit norm.

Anna: yep i ran `--norm l2`. Indexing pipeline used same cosine metric and HNSW params.

Vikram: can you check embedding magnitudes distribution? maybe int8 clamp killed high-magnitude dims. also check per-channel quantization vs global.

Anna: quick hist: ```
baseline mean L2=1.02 std=0.12
cetus-int8 mean L2=0.78 std=0.25
```

Vikram: that explains silhouette collapse, magnitudes vary more. Try rescaling (post-hoc normalize) and recompute recall. If recall improves -> quantization magnitude distortion.

Anna: re-ran with explicit post-normalize at index time -> recall@1=0.69 recall@5=0.84 recall@10=0.89 silhouette=0.27 mean_cosine_shift=-0.012

Tess: much better. so main issue is magnitude shift from int8 quantization. two follow-ups: 1) try per-channel quant (pq/perchannel) 2) run per-layer clamp tweaks and symmetric quantization.

Jordan: from infra side — if we keep cetus as int8 in Dedicated, we should canary at 5% and have a route to `beacon-embed-v2` fallback for low-confidence queries. also check that batchsize/threads during inference matches eval env (kv cache vs no-kv mismatch can change outputs slightly).

Anna: noted. I'll queue runs: per-channel int8, per-layer clamp, and an fp16 reference for the same eval set. also will run query-length stratified holdouts (short <8, mid 8-32, long >32).

eval-bot: automated report: `cetus-embed-6b` fp16 vs int8 quick table uploaded to /runs/3690001234/report.html. key: int8_perchannel expected to recover ~+0.02 recall@1 vs global-int8.

Vikram: if per-channel gets us within 0.01 recall@1 of baseline and silhouette >0.28 i'm comfortable with a limited canary. otherwise consider thresholding to use beacon for top-k where cosine confidence < 0.6.

Tess: also run a small clustering sanity on anchors — pick 1k anchors and measure nearest-neighbor label purity. will add to the run matrix.

Anna: plan: 1) run per-channel int8 + per-layer clamp (ETA ~2h) 2) run anchor purity and short-query stratification (ETA ~2h) 3) if metrics pass, push canary 5% with automatic fallback to beacon for low-confidence queries. Will post follow-up thread with numbers.

Jordan: sounds good. tag me when you push the canary so infra can watch latency and OOM. :thumbsup:

Vikram: one more: log the raw 512-d vectors for 100 failure cases (short queries that lost R@1) so we can inspect dimension-wise distortion.

Anna: will capture. thanks everyone. :rocket:
